data.content_ref: inline:The target claims the preference for higher-content theories is 'non-inductive' because it is made 'regardless of its truth probability.' But corroboration is explicitly defined in the mechanism as 'informational content retained after testing' — i.e., content that has survived severe tests. A preference grounded in what a theory has already survived is a preference grounded in its past observational record, which is precisely the inductive move (extrapolating from past performance to present preference). Declaring the preference 'regardless of truth probability' does not make it non-inductive; it merely renames the inductive basis as 'content retention.' The countercondition 'If acting on a high-content theory requires assuming its truth' is never discharged — the target provides no argument that one can act on or prefer a theory without any regard to its likelihood, rendering the central claim unsupported. Furthermore, the 'mechanism' is tautological: it states 'The reason this holds is that [the claim text], which is what the mechanism above establishes,' providing circular restatement rather than a derivational mechanism.
